f406.summary: Henri IV to Maisse at Venice, Chartres, 8 Feb 1593. In clear: he has answered every despatch and noted their dates, and has written to the Grand Seigneur and his ministers (Maisse may read the letter to Breves if he kept the copy of the cipher). In cipher (54 lines, from "Le surplus de voz lettres" to the end): Rome, Pisany's arrival in Italy and the war in Piedmont, with a letter and a further charge for Lesdiguieres; Gondi at Nancy with the King's passport; the King's journey to Tours and Saumur; a fund to keep the garrisons round Paris for a year; the duc de Mayenne gone to meet the foreign army under Count Charles while the Paris assembly waits; the King's declaration against the convocation. The French of the cipher part is the Brienne 13 copy; the cipher decrypts to it at 0.908 of letters.
f406.en:
Andrew Beling, with AI agents, 12 Nov 2026, of beling/readingf406.md. The clear part is WAINUT's translation (wainut/f406translation.md); the part in cipher is a new translation of the corrected copy. [?] = doubtful.

Monsieur de Maisse, I have always answered your despatches as I received them and noted their dates in my letters, so as not to leave you in doubt, and so that you could tell whether any of them had been lost.

Because of that uncertainty, I approve your practice of sending duplicates of the previous despatch with the most recent ones.

Since the last letters I wrote to you, I have received together yours of 26 December and 1 January; the latter reported the arrival with you of the ambassador[?] with his despatch.

f410.summary: Henri IV to Maisse, Mantes, 27/28 Apr 1593. In clear: he acknowledges Maisse's letters of 20 Feb, 7 and 23 Mar (one courier held by the duc de Nevers in Champagne) and assures him that his absence will cost him nothing. In cipher (93 lines, from "L'experience" to the end): experience has proved Maisse right about the affairs of Rome; the King will not yet recall Cardinal de Gondi or the marquis de Pisany; the Grand Seigneur's letters received; Lancosme to be carried off; the Chaous and the enterprise of Signa; 20,000 ecus for the presents of the Levant; Lesdiguieres and the title in Piedmont; the conference with the Paris assembly. The French of the cipher part is the Brienne 13 copy; the cipher decrypts to it at 0.908 of letters.
f410.en:
Andrew Beling, with AI agents, 12 Nov 2026, of beling/readingf410.md. The clear part is WAINUT's translation (wainut/f410translation.md); the part in cipher is a new translation of the corrected copy. [?] = doubtful.

Monsieur de Maisse, since my last letter of the 29th of last month, I have received yours of 20 February and of 7 and 23 March; the bearer of the last arrived sooner than the sieur de la Clielle[?], whom my cousin the duc de Nevers had kept with him for some days in Champagne.

You show me so clearly in your despatches the disposition and state of all things over there, even in what concerns my service, that I take much satisfaction from it, and I recognise more and more the usefulness that your good offices and the continual care you take there bring me.

system: Maisse's Cipher (1592-1593), the key Henri IV also sent to Savary de Breves: letter-shaped symbols for the letters, homophonic, with two-digit figures for a nomenclator of common words and names.
